changelog: 0.2.0-beta.4: Playback restored. The old providers are gone (Videasy's backend no longer exists and Stream Unity was retired), so streams now come from the MoviesAPI/VidSpark provider first with English subtitles, and the old chain stays behind it as a fallback. Verified on the exact bytes: release gate ALL_PASSED, TRON: Ares plays with a subtitle track.

0.2.0-beta.3: Embedded subtitles — captions are read from the stream itself when the source carries them (English first, 6+ languages on major titles), so subtitles keep working even when the external subtitle service is down. Poster fallback fixed (no more blank tiles) and title resolution fixed via Wikidata — titles such as Breaking Bad now resolve and play.
Oversized results on caption-rich titles are now size-budgeted for the app (no more failed resolves on big movies), and failed lookups report the real reason.

0.2.0-beta.2: First public beta of the Alpha Movies engine - three independent stream sources (Vidrock + Videasy + Stream Unity) behind one pipeline; every play returns multiple validated servers so a dead link no longer dead-ends. Posters now load via a cached image resolver; alternate-language audio sources are surfaced (labelled after English) and multi-audio streams show their track languages. Not the default movie source - install alongside Synthetiq Movies.
Owner-approved public beta for all-user testing; device-side certification and full playback QA are intentionally ongoing. Playback reports welcome in the Discord support channels.
1.1.1: Owner-approved public promotion of 1.1.0-beta.4; playback JavaScript unchanged.
Declare title audio availability so Sub-only titles such as Death Note do not offer unavailable Dub; preserve available server alternatives.
Standalone startup probes decoded 9/10 attempted audio modes across 8/10 selected titles.
Known issues remain: Pokemon XY returned no link, Gintama season 4 returned no episodes, and the Flutter Death Note stream check failed. See the release QA notes.

1.1.3: Playback restored. The source now hands back an opaque token instead of a direct URL and the module discarded it as "not a URL", so every provider looked dead. Tokens are expanded through the source's own proxy now, the live providers (wave/koto/megg) are tried first, and quality labels come from the stream itself (720p/360p) instead of a bare Auto. Verified on the exact bytes: release gate ALL_PASSED.

1.1.2: Owner-approved public release — restored playback: the player host shipped an encrypted stream descriptor (now decrypted in-module, cross-verified), and segments are classified by bytes (the CDN serves real video behind .jpg/webp labels) instead of content-type.
1.1.2: Resolution/validation caches and request dedupe keep normal browsing inside the source's request budget; verified live — streams resolve, zero 429s, app-runtime playback passes.
1.1.1: Owner-approved distribution of the unchanged testing package. Retains its beta label; not fully certified.
1.1.1: Checked server alternatives, recovered source-provided subtitle links and marker metadata where available; stop provider cascades during rate limits.
1.1.1: Long-distance seeks and downloads may remain slow. Some episodes fail resolution or decoding; audio-language and native seek certification remain incomplete. No app-code changes.

5.0.6-beta.3: Faster cached lookups with verified embed IDs, provider-scoped caches, safer fallback language checks and preserved external audio/subtitle playlists. Stops returning unrelated videos when embed metadata is unavailable. Owner-approved LIVE BETA: sampled media, runtime and regression checks passed; full certification and native phone acceptance remain pending. S2 retains the same opening-language detector flag observed on the previous live build. Existing source availability and backup-only-Dub limitations remain.

5.0.5-beta.7: Updates provider response and token handling, same-episode/audio checks and Retry-After handling. Experimental owner-requested live-test release: repeated-open failures and source/DNS availability remain unresolved. Do not treat this as a certified reopen fix.

5.0.5-beta.2: Restores stream resolution on the current rescue CDN routes (Sub and Dub). Fixes titles failing to load on the released app by raising the in-app probe budget (2MB to 4MB), extending the resolution deadline (3s to 5s), accepting size-capped reachability, and preferring routes without player-broken segment names. Subtitle tracks unchanged; verified on the released app runtime and S2.

5.0.4-beta.4: Fixed random skipping during playback (disguised .html segments mapped and served as genuine MPEG-TS video/mp2t). AES-CBC player stream descriptor decrypt support, improved fallback rate-limit handling, and normalized subtitle language tags.

5.0.4-beta.3: Vidhawk-independent AniKage rescue chain (labelled; used only when the primary has no verified media), MegaPlay descriptor decrypt fix, MAL-keyed rescue lookups, subtitle language tags. Fixes titles that went dark during the Vidhawk media-relay outage.

5.0.4-beta.3: Rescue routes pass the same positive media validation as primary routes and are never substituted across languages; episodes the rescue chain does not carry remain unavailable with an honest message.

1.1.2: Fixed double-audio playback reports (an extra song under the episode; audio continuing after pause on some titles) - the module now returns exactly one validated route per play so the app cannot start a second concurrent stream over the first; Sibnet MP4 stays primary with ansembed HLS as the per-episode fallback.
1.1.2: Certified before release: S2 runtime quick certification PASS with zero failure codes; release gate all-passed with 3/3 streams on first attempt.

1.0.0-beta.10: Fixes episodes that ended with no playable servers. The module read JSON responses through text(), and the app runtime returns an EMPTY text() for JSON (the parsed value is only exposed through json()) - so every Share4Max mirror list was lost, and only the HTML-based hosts could ever play. JSON is now read through json(); the Share4Max payload parser also accepts both payload shapes, and its phase is bounded to 9s so it cannot spend the whole episode budget.
1.0.0-beta.10: Identity assigned SP-VID-101-ANIME4UP (number 101; 100 belongs to Synthetiq-One in the video range - the signed pipeline rejects duplicates). Community module, first catalogue release.

1.0.0-beta.10: Verified on 6 live Share4Max shares (6/6 resolve after the fix, 0/6 before; avg 4.5s), 20/20 offline parser checks, 2,000 real episode URLs accepted. Community-built module, first catalogue release.

1.3.0-beta.9: Reduces repeated catalogue requests and rate-limit pressure, corrects unknown language availability after failed checks, and keeps HLS master streams when separate audio/caption tracks are present. Previous tests decoded 30 of 30 attempted routes; this is not a guarantee for every title, language or device.
1.3.0-beta.4: Playback restored after the site rotated its server lineup — adds UPNShare and Voe as first-class hosts so episodes keep resolving from the site itself.

1.3.0-beta.4: Independent rescue chain (EchoVideo / MegaPlay) now starts in parallel with the site hosts — if the site hosts and the previous fallback are down, the module still finds a verified stream instead of failing.
1.3.0-beta.4: Every offered server is byte-verified (real media segments) before it is shown, and dead relays are skipped in milliseconds.

1.3.0-beta.3: Reject the unplayable port-183 MP4Upload route in every runtime — the previous guard used the browser URL global, absent in-app and in the default test runner, so the route could still slip through and stall SUB playback (the reported One Piece S1E351 SUB failure).
1.3.0-beta.3: Labelled multi-language subtitle backbone failover for SUB mode with positive segment validation and real caption languages forwarded (English first); site hosts remain primary.

0.1.0-beta.4: Fixes user reports on downloads and playback - the module now defaults to its muxed video+audio engine (single stream whose timestamps were verified against the manifest across a full episode), so downloads keep their audio and A/V drift is gone; the AniPM engine remains selectable as the alternate server.

The home page is now a full browse experience: a Featured row plus paginated rows and an endless All Anime grid backed by the full 8,900+ title catalogue.

0.1.0-beta.2: First public release of the AniPM engine (ani.pm) - English anime with search, home feed and full episode lists (Sub/Dub flags on every episode). Two playback engines with server switcher: AniPM - adaptive-quality streams with English captions and opening/ending skip markers; MegaPlay - backup server. The module picks a reachable engine automatically per device. Certified: house tester 26/26, real app-runtime Sub+Dub pass, S2 quick Grade PASS.

Owner-approved all-user release. Notes: the AniPM engine serves iOS/iPadOS; other platforms resolve on MegaPlay automatically. A known app-side mid-play issue on some desktop platforms is being fixed in the app itself; Android and iOS playback are complete.

1.3.2: German subtitles fixed — subtitle options are verified before they are listed (empty placeholder tracks are never offered), German sorts first, and the verified tracks are attached to every server, so the picker works on the stream that is playing. The German option no longer appears and disappears between attempts.
1.3.2: Filemoon added — the site's fourth server now resolves (German and English variants), so every episode offers more working servers when VidMoly or Vidhawk is struggling.

1.3.1: Complete reliability certification pass across all platforms (100% / 150 checks passed across app-strict, mobile-ua, and desktop-ua). Verified VidMoly/VOE/Doodstream hoster racing with Vidhawk caption fallback.
1.3.0: Reliability rebuild - concurrent host racing takes the first verified route; one smart retry with cooldowns; new Doodstream resolver. No longer depends on a single working host.

changelog: 1.2.0: Fixes the episode failures reported on this source. The site repeats its players in a download section that can carry a mirror the server list omits - those extra mirrors are now used too, so episodes whose three listed servers were all deleted play again instead of reporting no link. No identity change.

1.1.0: Much faster home screen (the newest row and the three themed rows now load together instead of one after another: measured 8.4s -> 1.3s), plus verified server handling. Only the mirror family that can actually deliver video is offered: the site's DoodStream servers sit behind a bot wall, and its cybervynx servers were traced to playlists filled with ad images rather than video, so they are skipped instead of showing an option that cannot play. Source-side note: individual mirrors often go dead at the host - those episodes report honestly that no link is available rather than playing nothing.

1.0.0: First release of the CimaClub engine (w.cimacub.com) - Arabic subtitled movies, series and anime. The catalogue is read straight from the site's own WordPress API (search, newest-episode home rows and a paged feed), so titles and posters come from the source itself. Playback follows each episode's watch page to its MixDrop servers and resolves the player's signed mp4 url per play - those links expire in about four hours, so nothing is cached, and the mirror list cascades automatically until a live one answers. Not the default movie source; install alongside your others.

Owner-approved public release for all-user testing. Source-side notes: some mirror links are already dead at the host and get skipped automatically, and the alternative DoodStream servers sit behind a bot wall so they are not offered. Subtitles on this site are burned into the source video. Playback reports welcome in the Discord support channels.

1.0.5-beta.3: Search now groups every season of a show together, in order - searching a show name returns Season 1, 2, 3... (then movies/OVAs/specials) instead of a shuffled list, and result cards now show release years. Fixes the report that users had to type the show name with its season to reach the other seasons.

1.0.5-beta.2: Restores stream resolution on the current rescue CDN routes. Fixes titles failing to load on the released app by raising the in-app probe budget (2MB to 4MB), accepting size-capped reachability, and preferring routes without player-broken segment names. Sub/Dub and subtitles unchanged; verified on the released app runtime and S2.

1.0.4: Vidhawk-independent AniKage rescue source (labelled; used only when the primary has no verified media), byte-first segment validation, probe byte-cap fix for in-app playback, fair provider sweep and stalled-request caps. Fixes the module being fully dark during the Vidhawk media-relay outage.

1.0.4: Rescue routes pass the same positive media validation as primary routes and are never substituted across languages; episodes the rescue sources do not carry remain unavailable with an honest message.
Added the Fastest catalogue label
Runtime remains unchanged from 1.2.9

3.0.1: Owner-approved public release — fixed instant failures on strict HTTP clients (bodyless GET requests no longer carry an empty-string body); catalogue + real MP4 playback verified through the app runtime.
Bundle 80 certified release

presentation.purpose: TRfilm.Net catalogue, posters, search and discovery; full-film playback unverified

changelog: 1.0.0-beta.1: Search, movie details, poster shelves and site genres. Sampled films exposed trailers rather than verified full-film streams.
TEST-only cricket update for Player 9.0.91. Willow passed the actual native V9 Live player: sustained playback, pause/resume and fresh Go Live.

Supports validated wrapped Live video; removes false off-air detection based on image filenames. Broadcasts can include replays. General S2 Willow journey still fails outside the native path; no all-channel or Android certification.

1.3.4: Playback restored. The old embed page stopped exposing its player for most titles, so the module now resolves through the provider's own JSON player API (the page route stays as a fallback). Results also carry the primary URL, its headers and real quality labels (e.g. 536p) instead of a bare Auto. Verified on the exact bytes: release gate ALL_PASSED, 16/17 sampled titles, 12 subtitle tracks on a movie.
1.3.3: Fixes Fresh Retry getting stuck after earlier provider failures; prevents stale requests overwriting refreshed links; respects provider cooldowns. Keeps 1.3.2's faster verified-route startup.
Stricter film and season matching avoids substituting a different title or episode. Availability and quality still depend on the providers; this update does not make every title playable.
Owner-approved reliability release. Automated runtime and decoder evidence is recorded in the release notes; physical-device acceptance and full language certification remain incomplete.
Explicit provider servers and quality choices with source-specific subtitles and headers
Fix singleton-provider retries and expire cached video links; retain media and language gates

1.1.2: Owner-approved public release — titles that ship without artwork (e.g. upcoming 2026 films) no longer show the site's template logo; the real poster is resolved from each title's own page (cached, bounded). Playback code unchanged.

1.1.1: Owner-approved public release — restored playback: the backup provider dropped TMDB ids, so lookups now use an exact title+year identity match (never substitutes a different film); subtitle tracks are forwarded as absolute URLs, deduped per language, all languages kept.
1.1.1: Resolvers race so the first working source wins — a dead provider no longer delays playback (verified ~3.7s resolves with full subtitle sets).
1.1.0: Owner-approved beta.1 source unchanged; fresh playback links, episode ID fixes and provider-specific server/caption metadata.
1.1.0: Quality choices stay within the initial provider; other providers are available through Servers. Availability varies by title.
1.0.0: Official yFlix (yflix.ws) movies and TV series with adaptive 1080p/4K/720p HLS playback
